Synopsis:
    Houthi forces, with direct Iranian Revolutionary Guard guidance, have seized the strategic island of Perim at the Bab el-Mandeb Strait and key Red Sea coastal towns, threatening to give Iran control over a second critical global oil transit corridor — following the effective closure of the Strait of Hormuz six months prior after U.S.-Israeli airstrikes on Iran. Saudi crude output has already dropped to a 30-year low of 6 mbpd (-2.3 mbpd MoM). Oil prices are approaching $100/bbl. Satellite imagery suggests possible damage to Saudi Arabia's East-West pipeline — its key Hormuz bypass route. Trump has declined Saudi requests for U.S. strikes on Houthis. Diplomatic efforts are underway, with Gulf and Iranian foreign ministers set to meet in Oman Monday to negotiate a temporary Hormuz shipping deal.

Q02. Is the content confirming already known information or reporting very new/uncertain risks?
Risk score: 88/100 — The scenario described is highly escalatory and non-linear. Simultaneous closure of both Hormuz and Bab el-Mandeb, combined with possible damage to the Saudi East-West pipeline, represents a compounding tail-risk event far beyond baseline geopolitical assumptions. The diplomatic channel (Salalah meeting) introduces uncertainty but is unverified.
